title: Endpoints and email: which settings stop the attacks that actually land?
short: Make EDR block, not just alert, and put users on standard accounts this month; take every mail domain to DMARC reject within 90 days.
answer: This month, make EDR block on every laptop, remove users' local admin rights and turn on Microsoft's three standard attack surface reduction rules; this quarter, take your mail domains to DMARC reject and confirm every bank detail change by phone. Judge the rest by whether it stops pasted commands, fake sign-in pages or fake payment requests.
audience: IT teams in small and mid-size organizations managing Windows and Mac laptops, phones and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace mail, often without security staff

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Run EDR that blocks, on every device.
items.text: Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 lacks EDR; Defender for Business (in Business Premium) and Plan 2 have it[^mdb]. Turn on tamper protection, and on Macs move Defender's from audit mode to block[^tamper].

items.title: Take away local admin rights.
items.text: Entra join makes the joining user a local admin by default[^localadmin]; turn that off in the device registration policy or Autopilot profile. Manage the built-in admin with Windows LAPS, which needs only Intune Plan 1[^laps].

items.title: Turn on attack surface reduction rules.
items.text: Microsoft recommends block mode for its three standard protection rules without extensive testing, and audit mode first for the rest. The rules need Defender Antivirus in active mode[^asr].

items.title: Take every mail domain to DMARC enforcement.
items.text: Set up SPF and DKIM for every sender, then step DMARC from `p=none` via `p=quarantine` to `p=reject`, Microsoft's goal for every domain[^dmarcms]. Today, publish `v=DMARC1; p=reject;` on domains that never send mail, including onmicrosoft.com if unused[^dmarcms].

items.title: Confirm payment changes on a known number.
items.text: Call a known number before changing bank details or a payroll account. Microsoft saw over 46 million attacks posing as business contacts in a year, most opening with bland small talk[^mddr].

blocks.title: Roll out the device baseline in this order

items.title: Find the devices nobody manages.
items.text: Compare the device lists in Intune, Entra ID and your EDR console. Treat any device missing from one of them as unprotected until it is enrolled.

items.title: Replace or pay for what's out of support.
items.text: Windows 10 support ended on 14 October 2025. Commercial ESU costs $61 per device for the first year, doubles each year, lasts three years at most, and joining late means paying for the years you missed[^esu]. Office LTSC 2021 support ended on 13 October 2026[^officeeos]. Patch the rest within the patching sheet's deadlines.

items.title: Audit the other ASR rules, then block.
items.text: Run them in audit mode for a few weeks, add per-rule exclusions only for named business apps, then switch to block[^asr].

items.title: Add application control in audit mode.
items.text: In Intune's App Control for Business, trust Windows components and Store apps, apps with a good reputation and apps from the Intune managed installer. Apps installed before you enable the managed installer aren't tagged, so audit first[^appctl].

items.title: Encrypt, escrow the keys, then enforce.
items.text: Require BitLocker to store its recovery key in Entra ID before it encrypts[^bitlocker], and FileVault to escrow its key. Then make encryption a compliance rule and require compliant devices, as the passkeys and MFA sheet describes.

blocks.title: Device settings that close the common paths
items: **Block macro and script paths.** Office on Windows blocks macros in files from the internet by default, but the enforcing policy needs Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise[^macros]. Add the ASR rules against macro Win32 API calls, obfuscated scripts and scripts launching downloads[^asr].

**Limit what pasted commands can do.** ClickFix lures, which get users to paste a command into Run, Terminal or File Explorer, ran on over 1.1 million devices from February to early May 2026. Restrict PowerShell and JavaScript and enforce application control in user-writable folders[^mddr].
**Allow remote support tools for IT only.** Vishing callers get victims to grant access through one, then finish reconnaissance in two minutes or less[^mddr]. Block the rest with application control.

**Allowlist browser extensions.** Set Edge's ExtensionInstallBlocklist to `*` and list approved ones in ExtensionInstallAllowlist[^edgeext]. At the average company, over 15% of users had unauthorized AI extensions[^dbir].
**Give Macs the same baseline.** Atomic macOS Stealer topped the infostealer families Defender Experts saw[^mddr]. macOS has no ASR rules[^asr], so rely on EDR, FileVault and standard accounts.

**Protect work data on personal phones.** Intune app protection Level 2 blocks copy and paste to unmanaged apps, outdated OS versions and jailbroken devices. Require it in Conditional Access[^appprot].

blocks.title: Email settings against spoofing and fraud
items: **Turn on the preset policies.** Assign Microsoft's Standard preset security policy to everyone and Strict to admins, finance and executives; until you turn them on, they apply to no one[^preset]. In Google Workspace, turn on every option under Gmail **Safety**[^gws].
**Remove the Safe Links click-through.** Microsoft advises time-of-click URL checks without a user override; 89% to 96% of malicious attachments each month led to phishing pages, not malware[^mddr].
**Mark external mail.** `Set-ExternalInOutlook -Enabled $true` adds an External tag in Outlook on every platform[^exttag].

**Block automatic external forwarding.** Set the outbound spam policy to **Off - Forwarding is disabled**; the default, Automatic, varies by tenant. A compromised account can also add forwarding rules[^fwd]: see the incident response sheet.
**Reject Direct Send.** Run `Set-OrganizationConfig -RejectDirectSend $true` (off by default) once no scanner or app uses Direct Send[^directsend].
**Require TLS with MTA-STS.** Publish the policy in testing mode, then enforce. Exchange Online already checks other domains' policies on outbound mail[^mtasts].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **DMARC became a standards-track RFC.** RFC 9989 replaced RFC 7489 in May 2026 and swaps the `pct` tag for `t` (testing). It says domains whose users post to mailing lists should not publish `p=reject`, so check your reports for list traffic first[^rfc9989].
**Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro lost support.** They no longer get updates, and Enterprise 23H2 stops on 10 November 2026[^w11].

**Administrator protection shipped.** The October 2026 update turns it on where Microsoft's Windows security baselines apply. Microsoft says not to use it on LAPS-managed devices[^adminprot], so set the policy explicitly.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **More email phishing simulations.** Email phishing opened only 6% of Mandiant's 2025 intrusions, voice phishing 11%[^mtrends]. Spend the time on call-back rules for finance and the help desk.
**A second antivirus beside Defender.** ASR rules don't run while Defender Antivirus is in passive mode[^asr].
**DMARC forensic reports.** Microsoft 365 doesn't send them; start with aggregate reports only[^dmarcms].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Exclusions without an owner.** Excluded files run, and no ASR events are recorded for them[^asr]. Give each exclusion an owner and a review date.
**Trusting a whole share or site for macros.** Anyone who can add files there can add macros[^macros]. Sign the macros you need instead.
**Deleting a device before saving its keys.** Deleting it in Entra ID loses its LAPS password[^laps]; deleting its Intune object suspends BitLocker[^bitlocker].
**Changing bank details because an email thread says so.** Attackers reuse old threads to get bank accounts changed before a wire transfer[^dbir].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Use Business Premium's Defender for Business[^mdb] and the Standard email preset.
Make every user a standard user.
Use a DMARC reporting service and a call-back rule for every payment change.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Audit every ASR rule for a month, then block.
Pilot App Control for Business with the Intune managed installer.
Use Strict presets for finance and admins; enforce MTA-STS and reject Direct Send.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Enforce App Control on all workstations.
Handle elevation requests with Endpoint Privilege Management, not admin accounts.
Report weekly coverage: EDR blocking, ASR in block mode, encryption, supported OS.
